lead_with.title: A concrete fumarase offer, ready to forward
lead_with.text: Give Andrew a **one-page note** he can forward as-is: Enzymicals can supply **recombinant fumarase** (fumarate hydratase, EC 4.2.1.2) from a robust expression host, as crude lysate, purified or **immobilized** form, from gram samples to multi-kg/ton supply.

lead_with.title: Hit the food-grade price point
lead_with.text: Low cost comes from **high-titer recombinant expression**, minimal downstream (crude or lyophilized cell-free extract instead of purified enzyme) and **immobilization for reuse** across many batches. Offer a quick cost model once volume and spec are known.

lead_with.title: Ask for the direct intro
lead_with.text: Fumarase use in a workup depends on details (fumarate vs. malate direction, pH, temperature, solvent, impurities). Ask Andrew to connect David **directly** with the end user for a 20-minute technical call — faster than relaying questions.

industry.title: Fumarase is a classic industrial enzyme
industry.text: Fumarase converts fumaric acid into **L-malic acid**, a food acidulant (juices, jams) that holds roughly a tenth of the acidulant market after citric acid. Industry has long used immobilized microbial cells for this; research now targets immobilized fumarase for better stability.

industry.title: Immobilization is the cost lever
industry.text: Published work shows immobilized fumarase keeps about **2.5× more activity** than free enzyme after 30 days — the reuse that makes food-grade price points reachable.

industry.title: Enzymes in workups
industry.text: Using an enzyme to convert a by-product (e.g. residual fumarate) into an easier-to-remove compound is a growing green-chemistry tactic. The exact use here is **to be confirmed**.

talking_points: Thanks for passing this on — what is the **end user's application** (making L-malate, or removing fumarate/malate from a stream)?
What **volume** (kg enzyme or tons of substrate per year) and **target price** are they thinking of?
What **form** suits them: crude lysate, lyophilized powder, purified enzyme or **immobilized** (reusable)?
Process conditions: **pH, temperature, solvent**, substrate concentration — and any food or pharma grade needs?
Could you **introduce David directly** to the end user for a short technical call?
Side question: what is Chimera Bioscience — and does your own process work there ever need enzymes or expression support?
